chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a land of tax (kharaj), and I have become straitened by it.' He was silent for a while, then said, 'If our Qaim rises, your share in the land would be greater than it, and if our Qaim (peace be upon him) were to rise, Al-Astan would be more ideal than their pieces (of land).'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the land of kharaj and the rise of the Qaim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the eschatological transformation of land ownership under the Imam al-Mahdi (AS), contrasting the current burden of 'kharaj' (tax-liable) land with the abundance of the future era. The Imam’s pause signifies the weight of the prophecy, while the mention of 'Al-Astan' (often interpreted as the state treasury or the Imam's domain) being superior to fragmented private holdings underscores the centralization of wealth and justice in the Mahdist government. It serves as a practical encouragement for believers to endure current economic hardships with the hope of divine redistribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from his father who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For me is a land of taxes, and I am straitened by it, tired’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> was silent for a while, then said: ‘When our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises, your share in the land would be greater than it, and if our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> were to rise, Al Astaan would be more ideal than their pieces (of land)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from his father who has said the following: “

I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I had a piece of land of al-Kharaj which had caused to me great difficulties. He (the Imam) remained quiet for a while, then said, ‘On its coming (the time of the rise of al-Mahdiy with Divine Authority and Power) your share of the land will be greater than this and on such time ‘Ustan will be more ideal piece of land than their pieces.’”
